text: Opportunities arise. <break time="0.8s" /> When supply and demand for products or services. <break time="0.8s" /> Are not coordinated. <break time="0.8s" /> That is when markets are not as is often assumed. <break time="0.8s" /> In natural states of equilibrium. <break time="0.8s" /> Being off balance. <break time="0.8s" /> The market needs a little help. <break time="0.8s" /> And it is the entrepreneurial figure of action. <break time="0.8s" /> Rather than a regulator such as the state. <break time="0.8s" /> Who rises to the challenge. <break time="0.8s" /> Discovering opportunities when they come along. <break time="0.8s" /> In Kirzners view. <break time="0.8s" /> Entrepreneurs are alert to opportunities. <break time="0.8s" /> By discovering market errors. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as product or service shortages. <break time="0.8s" /> And exploit these. <break time="0.8s" /> By acquiring resources at lower prices. <break time="0.8s" /> Than they can later sell them for. <break time="0.8s" /> Thus, the entrepreneur is at all times. <break time="0.8s" /> Scanning the horizon. <break time="0.8s" /> As it were ready to make discoveries. <break time="0.8s" /> By taking advantage of price differences. <break time="0.8s" /> Entrepreneurs help move the market towards equilibrium. <break time="0.8s" /> By serving unmet needs. <break time="0.8s" /> And correcting resource misallocations. <break time="0.8s" /> One interesting aspect here is that the entrepreneur does not need to possess the means of production. <break time="0.8s" /> They only need to recognise and act on opportunities profiting from unexploited gain arbitrage. <break time="0.8s" /> Which means. <break time="0.8s" /> They are not just rational calculators. <break time="0.8s" /> But also risk takers. <break time="0.8s" /> Which in turn justifies their profits.
